issue: Distractor (d) 'Settlement of a tax dispute for a year-end tax year at an amount different from the accrual' is explained as a Type I (recognized) event, but under U.S. GAAP a post-balance-sheet development on an uncertain income tax position (including a settlement with the taxing authority) is treated as a nonrecognized subsequent event. So (d) is also a defensible answer to 'Which subsequent event is nonrecognized?', and the explanation teaches the wrong rule. The wording 'for a year-end tax year' is also garbled.
evidence: Blind answer c (agrees with key), but (d) can't be eliminated: ASC 740-10-25-15 bases subsequent recognition, derecognition and measurement of a tax position on the information available at the reporting date, and changes in judgment go in the period they occur. PwC Viewpoint 'IFRS and US GAAP: similarities and differences' §8.8 (uncertain tax positions) contrasts the two frameworks: under U.S. GAAP, developments affecting uncertain tax positions after the balance sheet date but before issuance, including information not available at the balance sheet date, are a non-adjusting (nonrecognized) subsequent event. Under IFRS (IAS 10) they can be adjusting. Item (d)'s explanation ('it settles a tax position that existed at year-end, so it is recognized') applies the IFRS/ASC 855 general logic, which ASC 740 overrides for income-tax positions. If 'tax dispute' instead means a non-income tax (e.g., a property-tax assessment, ASC 450), (d) would be Type I, so the stem is ambiguous either way.
source: ASC 740-10-25-15; ASC 855-10-25-1; PwC Viewpoint, IFRS and US GAAP: similarities and differences §8.8, https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/pwc/accounting_guides/ifrs_and_us_gaap_sim/ifrs_and_us_gaap_sim_US/chapter_8_liabilitie_US/88_uncertain_tax_pos_US.html
fix: Replace (d) with an unambiguous recognized event that is not an income-tax position, e.g., 'Receipt in February of the final invoice for legal services performed in December, $15,000 more than accrued' (explanation: evidence about a year-end liability, so adjust). Alternatively, if a tax item is wanted, make it a property-tax assessment for the current year and say so. Never use an income-tax uncertain-position settlement as a Type I example.

issue: Pure rule recall is labeled skill 'analysis', difficulty 3 (two levels too high). se-26 asks 'Through what date does an SEC filer evaluate subsequent events?' with no fact pattern. se-24 asks whether EPS is restated for a post-year-end 2-for-1 split.
evidence: se-26 is the same question as se-03 ('An SEC registrant evaluates subsequent events through which date?'), which is labeled remembering, difficulty 1; the cues.md near-duplicate scan pairs se-26 with se-03 (0.50) and se-11 (0.80). se-24 restates fc4 / key takeaway 4 verbatim and needs no fact analysis. Under the Blueprint, recall of a rule is Remembering & Understanding, and Analysis means examining relationships among facts to draw inferences. Both items count toward FAR's 35-45% Analysis target when they should count toward the 5-15% R&U target.
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill definitions; FAR skill allocation in content/sections/far.yaml
fix: Set skill 'remembering' and difficulty 1 on far-se-24 and far-se-26 (or delete se-26 as a duplicate of se-03).

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are one level off on single-rule classification items. se-17, se-18, se-20, se-21, se-22, se-23, se-25, se-27 and se-28 are labeled analysis, difficulty 3, but each applies one rule to one stated fact (application, difficulty 1-2). se-11 and se-15 are pure rule recall labeled application (they should be remembering). The labels are also inverted against their near-twins.
evidence: Twin comparisons: se-21 (stem says outright 'financial decline that existed at year-end') is analysis/3, while se-01 (the student must infer that the condition existed from 'worsening for a year') is application/2, and x3-23 (same fact as se-21) is application/2. se-22 (February fire) is analysis/3, but se-16 (January fire, same facts) is application/2. se-25 ($5M bonds) is analysis/3, but se-12 ($10M bonds) is application/1. se-28 (post-YE market decline) is analysis/3, but se-14 (same facts) is application/2. se-23 (lawsuit settled above accrual) is analysis/3, but se-13 (same) is application/2. Labeled practice+exam mix: 2 R / 15 App / 13 An (6.7/50/43%). Relabeled honestly, roughly 6 R (se-03, se-08, se-11, se-15, se-24, se-26) / 22 App / 2 An (se-02, se-09): 20/73/7%. The module's apparent fit to the FAR Analysis target (35-45%) is an artifact of the labels.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprints skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel se-17, se-18, se-20, se-21, se-22, se-23, se-25, se-27 and se-28 as application with difficulty 1-2, matching their twins. Relabel se-11 and se-15 as remembering. To raise genuine analysis content, add multi-event items (see the coverage finding) rather than inflating labels.

issue: Heavy redundancy: the same handful of facts is tested the same way 3-5 times, and several practice items are near-verbatim duplicates. One exam-pool item duplicates a practice item, which inflates mock scores.
evidence: Clusters (item counts include options in other items): (1) Pre-YE customer deterioration leading to post-YE bankruptcy, so adjust the allowance: se-01, se-10, se-21, x3-23, plus x3-15(c) and the lesson big-idea example. x3-23 ('a major customer files for bankruptcy because of financial difficulties that existed at year-end') is se-21 reworded, so a learner who has practiced se-21 sees the answer in the mock. (2) Post-YE bond issuance, so disclose: se-12 ($10M) and se-25 ($5M) differ only in amount, plus se-06(c) and x3-15(a). (3) Pre-YE lawsuit settled after YE, so adjust: chk1, se-04, se-13, se-23 (se-13 and se-23 are both 'settles above accrual'), plus x3-15(b). (4) Post-YE warehouse fire, so disclose: pre1 and se-16 are the identical 'January 20 warehouse fire' scenario, and se-22 repeats it in February (cues.md Jaccard 0.64). (5) SEC-filer date: se-03 and se-26. Non-SEC date: chk2 and se-11 (cues.md se-11~se-26 0.80). (6) Post-YE market decline: chk1(b), se-14, se-28. (7) Stock split: se-05, se-24. Cross-module: far-cont-27 (contingencies) repeats se-09's 'lawsuit filed after YE for a pre-YE event'. Meanwhile, gaps go untested (see the coverage finding).
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7 (same fact tested the same way more than about 3 times)
fix: Retire or rewrite the duplicates: se-16 (or change pre1), se-21, se-22, se-23, se-24, se-25, se-26 and se-28. Rewrite x3-23 so it does not mirror se-21 (e.g., an exam-style item with four mixed events). Reuse the slots for the untested sub-topics listed in the coverage finding.

issue: Trap labels don't match the misconception the distractor models. 'partial-computation' is used on non-computational distractors. Distractors that push recognition into the next period are labeled 'wrong-rule' instead of 'wrong-period'. Identical misconceptions carry different labels across twin items.
evidence: se-05(a) 'No effect; disclose the split only', se-24(c) 'Disclosed only' and se-13(a) 'A liability of $200,000, with disclosure' all model treating a recognized item as nonrecognized (wrong-classification), yet each is labeled partial-computation. The same misconception in se-23(a) is labeled wrong-rule. se-08(b) 'Only the date on which the event occurred' is an incomplete disclosure, not a computation. se-21(d) 'Record it next year only', se-24(b) 'Adjusted next year' and se-27(b) 'Record the loss in January' are labeled wrong-rule, while the same error in se-01(c), se-04(c) and se-13(c) is labeled wrong-period.
fix: se-05(a), se-13(a), se-24(c): wrong-classification. se-08(b): wrong-rule (or other). se-21(d), se-24(b), se-27(b): wrong-period.
